gap: No result ChatGPT got states that its top pick, the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic, cannot take an extra battery: EcoFlow's US page lists it as 'Expandable Battery: NO', so the 1,024 Wh it ships with is all the backup it will ever hold. The other limits are also missing: the compact Anker SOLIX C300 accepts only 11–28 V solar through an XT60 plug, does not work with Anker's own PS30 USB-C panel, and does not come with the solar cable it needs.
standout_why: I read three of the pages ChatGPT got. powerstationgearlab.com (cited) calls the DELTA 3 Plus expandable but says nothing about the Classic, which ChatGPT recommended, and it gives no voltage ranges, connectors or cables. flowersofvice.com (cited) gives only a 500 W max solar input and lists no V range, connector or cable. wattfolk.com names MC4 panels for the DELTA 3 and DELTA 3 Max but lists no input limits. I could not read urbangridbackup.com, the top cited result: WebFetch hit a self-signed certificate error and I was not allowed to fetch it with curl. That page may already have some of these facts, so this score assumes it does not.
decides: This supports the current page's split between small and large units and weakens ChatGPT's 'best overall' line. A renter who picks the DELTA 3 Classic for backup cannot add a battery later, so anyone who expects to need more than about 1 kWh should look at an expandable unit such as the BLUETTI AC180 already in the catalog. Expansion support for the AC180 still needs checking on BLUETTI's page; I only saw a rival page claim it. For the small kits, BLUETTI's 200 W solar cap on the Elite 30 V2 and Anker's 11–28 V limit on the C300 mean neither will run from a larger panel bought later. The C300 also needs its XT60 solar cable bought separately. The page should state these limits rather than change the pick.
